items.detail: Monday's rebound faded as the **Nasdaq** fell 1.48% to 23,733.54 Tuesday, and the S&P 500 slipped 0.50% to 7,201.09, its eighth loss in nine sessions.
items.why: Chip and server stocks gave back much of Monday's Nvidia-led surge as doubts about AI spending returned.

items.detail: **Nvidia** fell about 7% Tuesday, a day after its 31% jump, and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped roughly 9% after Monday's 14% surge.
items.why: Traders took quick profits on Huang's return because the export-control and accounting questions have not gone away.

items.detail: The **Dow** rose 0.85% to 50,018.70, its first close above 50,000, and Wednesday's October PCE inflation report is up next.
items.why: Money moved out of chips into healthcare and consumer staples, which make up more of the Dow than tech does.

items.detail: Asian chip markets erased Tuesday's rebound Wednesday, with Taiwan's Taiex down about **8%** early on and South Korea's KOSPI down about 5.6%.
items.why: Wall Street's renewed AI chip selloff and fresh US tariff threats hit TSMC, Samsung and SK Hynix hard.

items.detail: Indian markets reopened higher Wednesday after a Tuesday holiday, with the **Sensex** near 83,734 and the Nifty back around 25,729 by mid-morning.
items.why: Markets were shut for Guru Nanak Jayanti, so Wednesday's open caught up with Monday's global rebound.

items.detail: In the US, the **Russell 2000** rose 0.57% to 2,684.94 Tuesday, beating the Nasdaq by about two percentage points.
items.why: Investors moved out of AI chip stocks and into cheaper, more domestic companies, the same shift that lifted the Dow.

items.detail: **Bitcoin** slipped below $60,000 Tuesday, and November's spot ETF outflows hit a record **$4.71 billion**.
items.why: A fifth straight day of ETF withdrawals, led by BlackRock's IBIT, plus the tech selloff kept sellers in charge.

items.detail: **Ether** fell below **$1,690** Tuesday, giving up much of Monday's rebound above $1,800.
items.why: Spot ether ETFs posted a seventh straight day of outflows, and BTCS disclosed selling 27,300 ETH.

items.detail: **Solana** slipped to about **$72** as Monday's rally from near $65 faded well short of $80 resistance.
items.why: Solana ETFs had outflows again on Monday, which undercut the fund demand that had supported its outperformance.

items.detail: **Gold** gave up Monday's bounce, falling about 2% Tuesday and trading near **$3,550** early Wednesday, close to its 14-month low.
items.why: Consumer confidence jumped to 103.3, so traders fully priced in a December Fed hike, and AI losses forced some selling.

crossCuttingTheme: Monday's Nvidia relief rally unwound within a day, and the renewed chip selloff spread from Wall Street to Asia, while a surprise jump in consumer confidence locked in December hike bets and dragged gold down.
